notes: Check batch 2026-10-22-check-10 for shop-project with the skill: four runs (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), no opus, so the opus tier is unavailable in per_rule. All rc 0, model_id matches each tier, head 7fef5b5 with uncommitted true. skill_hash f7ec139c0d805a00f972075a62230bdba96c0ae318390191b74a4547827c106c in every result.json equals evals/tools/common.py folder_hash of the working tree's idiomatic-elixir/, so the runs read the uncommitted text graded here. skills_listed is 16 for haiku-1 and 29 for the other three. Every run read SKILL.md first.

Rules changed since the standard (2026-10-22-c at 3e3581d). Committed (git diff 3e3581d 7fef5b5): testing.md renamed ex_unit.md, the reference-table row widened, and Assert with patterns' == sentence reworded. Uncommitted (git diff 7fef5b5 -- idiomatic-elixir/ evals/cases/): the new Formatting bullet under "How to use this skill"; Before you finish step 1; and new text in "Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call" and "Use `do:` for a one-expression body...". Of the case's seven rules only Before you finish changed. Its step 1 now reads "Run `mix format path/to/file.ex` on any changed file you have not formatted since its last edit (see "Formatting" under "How to use this skill")". That sentence decides step 1. In all four runs each changed file was formatted after its last edit (by one file-scoped run after all edits), so step 1 holds in all four. The Formatting bullet is not a graded heading. Its timing is graded as the case's new check line, not under Before you finish. The other six rules are unchanged and graded to the 2026-10-22-c standard.

The new check, "`mix format` runs on each changed file right after its last edit to that file, not only in one project-wide run at the end", is met in 0 of 4 runs. Each run changed two files, lib/shop/cart.ex and test/shop/cart_test.exs, and ran `mix format` once, naming both files, after all its edits. No run ran a bare project-wide `mix format`; in 2026-10-22-c three of five did (haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2). In every run only the file edited last was formatted right after its last edit, and only because it happened to come last. Order per run (#n is the tool call): haiku-1: Write cart.ex (#7), Edit cart_test.exs x4 (#8-#11), Edit cart.ex (#12), then `mix format lib/shop/cart.ex test/shop/cart_test.exs 2>&1; git diff --no-index /dev/null /dev/null; ...compile; ...test` (#13), then `mix format --check-formatted` (#14). cart.ex was formatted right after its last edit; the test file was not, since the session edited cart.ex before formatting it. haiku-2: Write cart.ex (#5), Edit cart_test.exs x5 (#6-#10), then `mix format lib/shop/cart.ex test/shop/cart_test.exs && git diff --no-index /dev/null /dev/null; ...` (#11). cart.ex was formatted only at the end, after five test edits; the test file right after its last edit. sonnet-1: a refused python3 heredoc (#6) that would have written both files and then run `mix format lib/shop/cart.ex test/shop/cart_test.exs`, then Write cart.ex (#7), Edit cart_test.exs x2 (#8, #9), then `mix format lib/shop/cart.ex test/shop/cart_test.exs && mix test 2>&1 | tail -20` (#10). cart.ex was formatted only at the end; the test file right after its last edit. sonnet-2: a refused python3 heredoc (#8) with the same shape, then Edit cart.ex x2 (#10, #11), Edit cart_test.exs (#12), then `cd ... && mix format lib/shop/cart.ex test/shop/cart_test.exs && mix test 2>&1 | tail -20` (#13). cart.ex was formatted only at the end; the test file right after its last edit.

Reading the formatter's output: in no run did the formatter change anything. I replayed every Write and Edit in each transcript onto the case's starting files and compared the result with the run's final files. All eight files are identical, so there was no change to read. `mix format` prints nothing, and no run looked at a real diff. haiku-1 and haiku-2 both appended `git diff --no-index /dev/null /dev/null`, which compares nothing and prints nothing. haiku-2 then wrote "The skill says to check what `mix format` changed, so I'll look for a `do:` body it moved onto its own line" and printed lines 95-130 of cart.ex with sed (#13); the awk check for lines over 98 characters that it chained first (#12) was refused. haiku-1 later read lines 1-20 of cart.ex (#16), with no stated link to formatting. sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 did nothing after formatting except run tests and Credo. One related observation: sonnet-1's test Edit (#9) wrote a long test head already in the formatter's wrapped shape, `test "takes 10% off the subtotal but not the shipping with SAVE10", %{` / `cart: cart,` / `prices: prices` / `} do` (test lines 79-82). Its refused draft had it on one line. The Formatting bullet says a line the formatter breaks is one to rewrite rather than accept. Here the session wrote the broken shape itself, so the formatter had nothing to break. No graded rule covers a test head, so I did not count it.

Before you finish, what each session ran (0 of 4 violated). haiku-1: after its last edit, `mix format lib/shop/cart.ex test/shop/cart_test.exs`, `mix compile --warnings-as-errors --force` and a full `mix test` (17 passed), then `mix credo --strict` (no issues) and `mix format --check-formatted`. haiku-2: one chain after its last edit, with format, `mix compile --warnings-as-errors --force`, a full `mix test` (15 passed) and `mix credo --strict` (no issues). sonnet-1: `mix format <both files> && mix test` (19 passed; the output shows `==> shop / Compiling 1 file (.ex) / Generated shop app` with no warnings), then `mix credo --strict` (no issues). sonnet-2: the same shape (21 passed, no warnings), then `mix credo --strict` (no issues). Neither Sonnet run ran a separate `mix compile`; the separate compile was only in sonnet-1's refused heredoc. Following the judgment call in 2026-10-22-c (its sonnet-2) and 2026-10-22-b, I count a mix test that compiled the app with no warnings as clean. A stricter reading that requires the literal command would make Sonnet violated. In every run the last mix test was the full suite, with no edit after it. No run used a single-file or :line test form.

Chain fallible steps with `with`: sonnet-1 is the only violation. It has one-step `with` blocks in two public functions: apply_code/2 at line 70 and total_price/2 at line 94. Each function's only fallible call is the first step and its body builds the result, the shape the rule's third paragraph names. This is the same shape that check-9's sonnet-2 had. sonnet-2's refused python3 draft had a one-step `with` in apply_code/2. The Edits that replaced the draft wrote `case` (lines 78-81), so the output does not break the rule, as with 2026-10-22-c's sonnet-2. haiku-1 and haiku-2 write no `with` and call no fallible helper. haiku-1 checks `if code in @discount_codes`; haiku-2 uses `case normalized do known when known in @codes -> ...`.

Other rules, graded to the 2026-10-22-c standard. Both Haiku runs keep the code as a string checked against a literal list (haiku-1 `@discount_codes ["SAVE10", "FREESHIP"]`, haiku-2 `@codes ["SAVE10", "FREESHIP"]`). That counts as clean under the atoms rule, as the case's checks allow and as earlier grades counted it. Both Sonnet runs map strings to atoms with `parse_code/1` clauses. defstruct: haiku-1 `[:items, :code]`, haiku-2 `[:items, :discount_code]`, sonnet-1 `[:items, :discount]` and sonnet-2 `[:discount, items: %{}]` (a bare atom for the nil default and a keyword for a real default). All four are clean. Map.put/3 on the inner items map inside `%{cart | items: ...}` is not what the struct rule forbids. A total that raises KeyError on an unpriced SKU counts as clean under the return-tuple rule when its @doc says so (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-2); sonnet-1 returns {:error, {:unknown_sku, sku}}. I found no break of the reworded do: rule or multi-line-argument rule. Every function that mixes do: and block clauses sets the block clause apart with a blank line, and no do: body is wrapped. Test bodies follow Assert with patterns in all four runs: every arrange match takes assert, and the value under test is on the left of ==. Each Haiku run pipes two steps on one line (haiku-1 line 54 `input |> String.trim() |> String.upcase()`, haiku-2 line 51 `code |> String.trim() |> String.upcase()`), listed under the pipeline rule as in earlier grades.

Expected reads: all four runs added tests and all four read ex_unit.md before their first edit. haiku-1 used Read (#4), haiku-2 cat (#4), sonnet-1 Read (#4, after a refused cat) and sonnet-2 Read (#4, after two refused cats). The check is met 4 of 4.

Verified in scratch copies of each run's project (copied with the case's .formatter.exs, then mix deps.get). mix format --check-formatted, mix compile --force --warnings-as-errors (rc 0, no warnings), mix credo --strict (no issues) and mix test pass in all four: haiku-1 17 (2 doctests), haiku-2 15, sonnet-1 19 (3 doctests), sonnet-2 21 (4 doctests). A mix run probe with 2 x APPLE at 100 cents gives 699, 679 with SAVE10 and 200 with FREESHIP in all four (sonnet-1 as {:ok, cents}). The Haiku runs trim and upcase the code and replace an earlier code; the Sonnet runs are case-sensitive and reject a second code with {:error, :code_already_applied}. Removing 5 of 2 units empties the items. BOGUS returns an atom or tagged-tuple reason. An unpriced SKU raises KeyError, except in sonnet-1, which returns {:error, {:unknown_sku, "KIWI"}}. No lib file has String.to_atom/1 or a float.
